Serial constraints cleared: nothing in flight touches `packages/cli`. Lane siblings #8039 / #8264 land in `packages/rest`, #8087 in `packages/runtime` + `packages/types` — all disjoint. No open PR touches `serve.ts` at claim time.

**Authorization — maintainer direct-dispatch channel.** This card carried no pm-state (triage had not queued it), so it was not dispatchable under the ordinary rule. The maintainer directed it in a live PM session, verbatim:

> 派

Under the 2026-08-10 standing authorization, a maintainer-directed PM session routes directly, with the instruction quoted in the audit comment; this applies only to the card explicitly directed. `pm:dispatched` here therefore comes from that instruction, **not** from a triage grading — the triage seat should still record its own `type`/grading judgement if it disagrees. `priority:p1` is left exactly as filed; ⛔ this seat does not produce priority labels.

**Premise re-verified on `origin/main` @ `cb43296ef`.** The gating block is real and reads as the card describes, but **the card's line number has moved** (`:1652` → the block now sits at `:1725-1736`), so the arm must be located by text.

⚠️ **Two findings from the premise check that change what this card is, both handed to the dev as falsifiable assumptions rather than conclusions:**

1. **There is a SECOND skip condition the card does not mention, and it is checked first.** `if (!isRuntimeHostKernel)` wraps the entire block — the wiring is skipped outright when `ObjectOSEnvironmentPlugin` is present, because "the cloud distribution (objectos-stack) wires its own MarketplaceProxyPlugin on the host kernel, so auto-wiring here would double-mount". The measured deployment is `objectos-ee`, which may well be exactly that. If so, `OS_CLOUD_URL=off` is **not** the cause, the diagnosis on this card is wrong, and the fix is somewhere else entirely — possibly in the `cloud` repo. That question is the dev's first task, before any edit.
2. **"Mounting it unconditionally therefore costs nothing" is contradicted by the code's own comment.** The gate is documented as deliberate: `OS_CLOUD_URL=off -> nothing mounts, preserving the vanilla marketplace-less `objectstack dev``. And each plugin "self-registers its own Setup nav bundle in `start()`" — so unconditional mounting adds a Setup nav entry to every plain `objectstack dev` app. That is a real cost on a surface the card did not weigh, and the fix has to reconcile the offline-install need with the vanilla-dev intent rather than assume no conflict.

Also noted: the second symptom (`features.installLocal: true` with no endpoint) cannot come from the skipped `RuntimeConfigPlugin` — that plugin lives in `packages/cloud-connection` and is registered *inside* the skipped block. Whatever serves `/runtime/config` in the EE image is a different producer, plausibly in the `cloud` repo. If it lands there it is a separate card in that repo with a `Blocked-by:` link, ⛔ not folded in here.

## ACCEPT — PR #8358

Reviewed against the diff and `origin/main`, not the report. 4 files, 476 insertions / 6 deletions; the six deletions are the condition lines being split. Scope is exactly the claimed surface plus tests.

**Both dispatch doubts were tested first, and both moved the work — which is the point of writing them down.**

1. **My "maybe the other guard fired" doubt: falsified, and not by reading alone.** `ObjectOSEnvironmentPlugin` is constructed only by `createObjectOSStack`, called only on the EE config's `OS_MULTI_TENANT` branch; the measured box is `OS_MODE=standalone` multi-**org**, a different axis, so `isRuntimeHostKernel` is false. Then corroborated from the *field data*: the measured `autoPublishAiBuilds: true` can only come from the cloud-wired `RuntimeConfigPlugin` subclass (the open plugin's static default is `false`), which only the single-environment branch mounts — so the branch demonstrably ran. Two independent routes to the same conclusion, one of them using the reporter's own evidence. The card's diagnosis stands.
2. **My "unconditional mounting costs a nav entry" doubt: partly falsified, and it changed the design.** A plain `objectstack dev` sets no `OS_CLOUD_URL`, so `resolveCloudUrl()` returns the truthy `DEFAULT_CLOUD_URL` — vanilla dev has been mounting install-local and its nav entry all along and is byte-identical after this change. Only explicit opt-outs (`off`/`none`/`local`/`disabled`) are affected, which is precisely the population the card is about. My concern was worth raising and empirically empty; the honest version of the vanilla-dev intent is preserved rather than overridden.

**The trap it found is worth more than the fix.** The obvious spelling — reuse the empty `marketplaceUrl` already in scope — would have been silently catastrophic: `resolveCloudUrl()` reads `''` as *unset* and substitutes the public `DEFAULT_CLOUD_URL`, so an air-gapped runtime's catalog branch would have been pointed at `cloud.objectos.ai`, the exact opposite of what `off` requested, invisible until a box with no egress hangs. `static readonly OFFLINE_CONTROL_PLANE = 'off'` is a named constant specifically so a test asserts the property instead of a comment claiming it — verified in the diff, along with the pin that turns red when it is changed back to `''`. The second guard (`kernel.use` keys by name, so an unguarded mount would silently *replace* a host's own URL-configured install-local) is the same class of catch.

**Reverse verification, direction predicted before running, from the committed state**: restoring the pre-fix rule turns exactly 1 of 9 red (the offline-mount pin) with 8 green; changing the sentinel to `''` turns the trap pin red reporting `expected 'https://cloud.objectos.ai' to be ''`. Both observed as predicted, then restored byte-identically.

**All four filed cards verified to exist**, not merely described: #8355 (the README wiring example that *propagated* this P1 into the EE config — the vector, which is the most useful of the four), #8356, #8357 (`finding`), and **objectstack-ai/cloud#1287** with a `Blocked-by` link, which is the contract-first cross-repo split done correctly.

---

### Ruling on open question 1 — **option A, as shipped.**

`features.marketplace` stays out of this PR; the fix lands at its source in #8356. Your reasoning is right and I am adopting it rather than restating it: **B trades the reported bug for its mirror image** — this card's own complaint is a flag advertising a route that 404s, and B would ship exactly that one key over. **C repeats the mechanism that caused the P1**: "every host must remember to keep the flag in step" is what the EE config and the package README both failed to do. A puts the answer in the component that can actually know it. Not a maintainer-floor call — it widens no contract and adds no public surface; it restores declared = enforced.

Consequence stated plainly so it is not discovered later: **a cloud-less framework runtime now has a working install-local route the Console cannot yet discover.** That is a strictly better state than the reported one (route missing entirely) and is tracked with an acceptance list at #8356.

### Ruling on open question 2 — **`Part of` stays, and this card does NOT close on merge.**

You applied the rule correctly and were right to flag the consequence. My answer is not "switch to `Fixes`":

This card's shape is the same as #7644's — **the fix is at HEAD, and the reporter measured a published image.** `objectos-ee` runs `ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectos-ee@sha256:c93b4937…` (4.0.5-rc.1); nothing this PR does reaches that deployment until an image carries it. Closing on merge would tell the filer their blocked HotCRM install is unblocked when the box they measured is byte-identical to before.

So on merge I move this to **`pm:on-hold` with a mechanically checkable restart condition** — an EE image built from a CLI containing this change — rather than either closing it or leaving it in the dispatchable pool. That keeps the P1 honest: the code half is done and reviewed, the verification half is waiting on a release, and it is nobody's dispatchable work in between. The residual scope items are independently carried by cloud#1287 and #8356 regardless.

**Landing**: path face clean (no `docs/adr/**`, no `skills/**`) → normal route. Ready-flip and queue once the gate jobs converge.

**Restart condition (mechanically checkable):** an `objectos-ee` image whose bundled `@objectstack/cli` contains `Serve.OFFLINE_CONTROL_PLANE`. On such an image the original reproduction should flip:

```
GET  /api/v1/marketplace/install-local   # expect: not 404
POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local   # expect: not 404
os package install ./dist/objectstack.json
```

If it still 404s on an image that carries the constant, reopen — that would be a second, distinct defect and the diagnosis on this card would need re-doing.

### Residual scope, owned elsewhere — not lost, not this card's

Your closing line — "whichever component reports `features.installLocal` should report what is actually mounted" — was outside the dispatched file surface and is carried by two cards, both filed with backlinks:

- **objectstack-ai/cloud#1287** (`Blocked-by` this card) — the actual producer of the flag on the EE image: `apps/objectos-ee/objectstack.config.ts` mounts `RuntimeConfigPlugin({ installLocal: true })` *outside* the ternary holding the plugin. On your image this merge makes that flag truthful again, but only because that lower layer backfills it — which is exactly what that card fixes properly.
- **#8356** — `RuntimeConfigPlugin` hardcodes `features.marketplace: true`. This is why #8358 mounts install-local **alone** on a cloud-less runtime: mounting runtime-config there too would have restored the Console's knowledge of install-local at the price of asserting a browse capability that is definitively absent — trading your reported bug for its mirror image. Consequence stated plainly: a cloud-less framework runtime now has a working install-local route the Console cannot yet discover. Strictly better than the route not existing, and tracked with an acceptance list.

Also filed from this investigation: **#8355** — the `cloud-connection` README's wiring example gates install-local on the cloud URL, contradicting its own prose one paragraph below, and the EE config is a faithful copy of that recipe. That README is the vector that propagated this P1, and is the highest-leverage of the follow-ups. **#8357** (`finding`) — the connected arm can still silently replace a host's own marketplace plugins.

Thanks for the report — the measurements in it (closed-off alternatives, the OpenAPI check, `OS_ARTIFACT_PATH` taking a single artifact) are what made this diagnosable in one pass, and the `autoPublishAiBuilds: true` in your `/runtime/config` dump turned out to be the evidence that settled which of the two guards had actually skipped the mount.

## H11 re-check, round 34 — predicate REPAIRED. Hold state, grade and substance all unchanged.

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`. The 2026-08-24T08:00Z sweep raised **H11** on this card again (bug parked in `pm:on-hold`, now ~11d against a 7d threshold). The previous H11 discharge (`5355407715`, round 30) found the exit predicate unrunnable and declined to fix it. Four days later it is still unrunnable and the row has fired again — a report that changes nothing is not a discharge, so this time it is repaired.

### What was wrong

The body's `Restart-when:` line named the image as `ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectos-ee:` — **a trailing colon with no tag**.
